name: Proto-fascism
summary: Proto-fascism covers the radical nationalist, anti-liberal and anti-socialist movements and thinkers before fascism that shaped it. They put the nation above the individual and class, rejected parliamentary democracy, glorified violence and war, favoured strong authority and corporatist class collaboration, and often scapegoated minorities, though usually without totalitarian ambition.
scope: Based mainly on the Italian pre-fascist right (Italian Nationalist Association, Corradini's proletarian nation, Rocco's corporatism, Marinetti's Futurism) and French integral nationalism (Maurras, Action Francaise). Other cases listed in the Wikipedia article (Voelkisch, Freikorps, Black Hundreds, Spanish and Japanese movements) inform it less; it is a family label, so many answers are inferred and low confidence.

sources.usedFor: Corradini: nationalism as socialism of nations, class collaboration, imperialist war, iron discipline.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Corradini-era nationalists cared about national strength and class peace, but no source documents a health-care position; inferred as indifferent.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage floors imposed by statute are not in the nationalist programme; the corporatist model had state-supervised bodies set wages instead, so a mild no is inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The proletarian-nation outlook subordinated markets to national strength and rejected liberal economics, though it welcomed productive private enterprise.

public-ownership.rationale: The ANI wanted an industrial state strong enough to compete with empires, via producers and the state together rather than nationalisation; inferred mild opposition.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Productive owners were counted among the moral proletariat who should lead the nation, so soaking the wealthy was not a programme; inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Free unions were seen as vehicles of class conflict and internationalism; the ANI wanted unions folded into state corporate bodies that end class struggle.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private property was kept under corporatism but subordinated to the nation, so adherents lean neither way strongly.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corradini attacked foreign plutocracies but welcomed domestic entrepreneurs; no clear stance on regulation of corporations as such.

cut-welfare.rationale: The sources do not address welfare; national-strength concerns pull both ways.

worker-ownership.rationale: Corradini rejected socialism and worker takeover, holding that owners and entrepreneurs were productive leaders alongside workers.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Authoritarian anti-leftist movements such as the Freikorps and White Guards put order against subversion first; inferred as agreeing.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No documented position; the cult of discipline, virility and national vigour suggests disapproval, though Futurists were bohemian.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Movements that scapegoated minorities and glorified violence rejected liberal limits on such speech and would not accept it being restricted.

strong-leader.rationale: Favouring a single leader with absolute power is listed as a shared trait of proto-fascist movements.

state-harmful.rationale: Nationalists wanted a strong authoritarian, corporate state; anarchist rejection of the state is opposed to everything they held.

limit-guns.rationale: Paramilitary leagues and veterans' bands valued armed force; no documented stance, inferred against strict limits for loyal citizens.

empower-police-military.rationale: The ANI stressed militarism, discipline and imperial power, and favoured authority against subversion.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from moralism-versus-virility mix; no source addresses it, so low-confidence mild no.

decide-locally.rationale: The ANI turned authoritarian and centralist around the nation-state; only Maurras favoured regional privilege under a monarchy, so a mild no.

rehabilitation.rationale: Movements prizing discipline and violence favoured toughness over rehabilitation; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Maurras defended family as an organic unit and order and hierarchy generally; the Futurists dissented but the mainstream is traditional.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Traditionalist, Catholic and hierarchical integral nationalism and the militarist right would reject it; not explicit, inferred from core values.

abortion-legal.rationale: National-vitality and Catholic order concerns suggest opposition; not directly documented.

more-religion-public.rationale: Maurras wanted the Church as an instrument of order though he was not personally devout; the Futurists and many Italian nationalists were secular, so split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Scapegoating of minorities and ethnic nationalism are shared traits; remedial racial programmes contradict them.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The Futurist manifesto disdains women and feminism and stresses virility; inferred rejection of social constructionism.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Integral nationalism puts the nation as highest value and defends its tradition and culture.

gradual-change.rationale: These movements prized violence, revolt and radical rebirth over gradualism, though Maurras counter-revolution respected old institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Maurras treated foreigners as "Anti-France" who cannot be integrated, and xenophobia was common.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalists rejected internationalism and wanted national power and empire.

free-trade.rationale: Competing against imperial powers led nationalists to industrial state strength and protection rather than liberal free trade.

nation-first.rationale: The nation is the highest absolute value to which other interests are subordinated.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Subordinating humanitarianism to the nation implies force abroad serves national interest, not human rights.

open-borders.rationale: Integral nationalists regard foreigners as unassimilable and the nation as an exclusive community.

limit-growth.rationale: The ANI wanted industrial strength for empire, so limiting growth runs against it; environmental views were not addressed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate was anachronistic; inferred opposition from priority on industrial and national power.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Futurists celebrated machinery and speed while Maurras traditionalists did not; weighted toward the Futurist and industrial-nationalist side.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; industrial power favours it, traditional ruralists would not.

revolution-justified.rationale: Movements such as the Arditi, Freikorps and Sorel followers glorified revolt and violence, although mostly against the left.

experts-over-public.rationale: Corporatist assemblies of producers imply technocratic elements, but the leader and nation are supreme.

central-planning.rationale: The ANI corporatism coordinated private producers under the state rather than abolishing markets.

socialized-markets.rationale: Corradini rejected socialism, and favoured productive owners and entrepreneurs leading the nation.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed by any source; neutral.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from respect for productive owners and family continuity.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; inferred opposition from emphasis on production, discipline and duty.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Building an industrial state able to compete with imperial powers implied protection of domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The ANI sought a state-guided industrial build-up for imperial competition.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Maurras valued agrarian petite property in traditional France while industrial nationalists did not; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Corradini opposed socialism and counted owners and workers as producers within nation.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; strong-state outlook suggests opposition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Alfredo Rocco corporate state with assembly of unions and economic bodies was adopted by the ANI from 1914.

one-party-rule.rationale: Single leader with absolute power and anti-parliamentarism are shared traits, though proto-fascists generally lacked totalitarian ambition.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The ANI supported the monarchy and Maurras held monarchy essential to the French nation.

democracy-best.rationale: Anti-liberalism and anti-parliamentarism are core features of proto-fascist movements.

direct-votes.rationale: Plebiscitary mass politics was not their method; they rejected parliamentary democracy and favoured leader authority.

workers-councils.rationale: The ANI wanted corporate bodies with state recognition, not socialist workers' councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Integral nationalism places the unity of the nation first.

natural-rulers.rationale: Order and hierarchy are stressed and elite leadership over mass democracy was typical.

political-violence-never.rationale: Glorification of violence is a listed shared trait, and Sorel and the Arditi celebrated it.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Futurist manifesto praises war as a cleansing force and the ANI sought imperial war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Maurras wanted the Church as instrument of the state while Futurist and secular nationalists did not; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Maurras valued Catholicism for social order but his Action Française was not theocratic; mild no.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defence and justice are core state functions for an authoritarian, militarist nationalism.

military-superiority.rationale: The ANI stressed militarism, imperialism and power competition with great powers.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Ethnic and integral nationalism, including Völkisch thought, is central, though Maurras' was more cultural than racial.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Corradini replaced class struggle with national struggle between proletarian and plutocratic nations.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy and order are valued and equality is rejected.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from ethnic and territorial nationalism.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Proto-fascist nationalists were imperialist and wanted their own colonies.

civilizational-union.rationale: Integral nationalism prioritises the single nation over supranational unions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Individual interest was subordinated to national and producer solidarity.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The individual is subordinated to the nation as absolute value.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Blood and Soil romanticism valued land but not nature as such; no clear position.

limit-population.rationale: The proletarian-nation argument welcomed Italian numbers as strength and emigrants, and nationalists feared decline.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Futurists and the ANI embraced industry; only romantic Völkisch strands lamented it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Futurism celebrated speed, machinery and disruption of the old.

human-enhancement.rationale: Futurist cult of the machine and vigour suggests interest, but unaddressed; neutral.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; will and leadership over calculation suggests rejection.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; state authority over individual privacy suggests rejection.

restore-past-order.rationale: Maurras sought restoration of an old order while Futurists and the ANI sought modernist rebirth; adherents split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Will and myth were put above reason and the nation as ideological absolute.

direct-action.rationale: Freikorps, Arditi and Sorel believed in violent mass action against parliaments.

means-match-ends.rationale: The violent means of these movements did not mirror any ideal society; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Futurists and industrial nationalists embraced modernity and power.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Corporatism is built on organised producers in their functions.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Corradini rejected socialism and class levelling in favour of national competition.

production-for-use.rationale: Corporatist production served national power while keeping private enterprise.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Owners and entrepreneurs were counted as productive, so profit as exploitation was rejected.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Corradini rejected revolutionary socialism and class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Maurrasian ruralism and nationalists upheld small proprietors, and rejected socialist collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Corradini saw imperialist war as good against plutocracies, not as a capitalist evil to abolish.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state-centred, authoritarian nationalism holds taxation legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: The individual is subordinated to the nation, not protected by a harm principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individual interests are subordinated to the nation and organic communities.

conscription.rationale: Militarism and discipline were central to the ANI.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Exit-over-voice is a liberal market argument contrary to national loyalty.

state-as-business.rationale: The nation as organic and sacred whole is not a customer-served firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Corporatists claimed social provisions through the state but not as liberty; not addressed.

media-academia-power.rationale: Anti-intellectual and anti-liberal rhetoric existed, but no documented claim about media power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Eugenics and racial thinking appear in Finnish White Guard and German Völkisch strands, though Maurras and Italian nationalists were not biological racists.

organic-representation.rationale: The ANI proposed an assembly of unions and economic bodies instead of parliament.

total-state.rationale: Proto-fascists generally lacked totalitarian ambitions, even while favouring a strong corporate state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Decadence and rebirth underpin the movements, from Maurras decline narrative to Futurist renewal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The ANI irredentism and imperialism sought territory and empire.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The ANI backed a modern monarchy and corporate state, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Modern industrial nationalists did not seek serfdom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Will over reason and myth have some affinity, but no stated position on knowledge.

universal-morality.rationale: Nation as highest value and rejection of Enlightenment universalism.

single-common-good.rationale: Class conflict was to be replaced by national unity and a single national interest.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Antisemitism was common in these movements, so support for a Jewish state is unlikely, though expulsionist logic could favour it; low.

revive-national-language.rationale: Cultural nationalism favours it in places, but unaddressed.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporatist hierarchy was designed to end class conflict by state, not by worker votes.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed, and state control of education pulls the other way.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: No source documents a fiscal-policy stance; military and imperial spending pulled toward deficits, orthodoxy the other way.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economy was subordinated to the nation by the state.

rule-by-example.rationale: Movements stressed force and a strong leader, not example over punishment.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationalists claimed it for their nation, as in Italian irredentism, but not for others, hence only moderate.

force-without-un.rationale: Imperialist and militarist nationalism accepts force abroad without international consent.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Willpower took priority over reason in integral nationalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Exclusion of foreigners makes reserving benefits for citizens likely, though welfare itself was not addressed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Emphasis on producers and duty suggests agreement; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Corradini and the ANI corporatism replaced class struggle with national producer unity.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Marinetti called for destroying museums and libraries, but Maurras and most nationalists defended heritage; split.

dominated-front.rationale: The proletarian-nation idea cast poor nations against plutocracies, but a common front among them was not proposed.

workers-nation.rationale: Corradini put the working class into the nation, against socialist internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Futurist manifesto expresses contempt for women and feminism, and traditionalists agreed on distinct roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Not documented; productive owners and finance capital distinct but no ban proposed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The article lists Jim Crow among American roots, but the European core did not propose it; split.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The nation-state was seen as the union of classes, not the tool of one.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Maurras held that Metics could never be integrated, so assimilation is not the answer; many nationalists demanded it.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy of elites is a late concept; antisemitic strands had conspiracy ideas but no documented claim.

national-mission.rationale: Imperial nationalism implies a civilizing mission, though not necessarily of its form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Disdain for women and feminism implies rejecting the claim.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-parliamentary and populist attacks on liberal political elites were central, as in the Dreyfus era.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics appears in some strands such as the Finnish White Guard figure Pihkala, but not documented for the Italian core.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Freikorps and White Guard violence against leftists was admired by these movements.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A strong corporate and imperial state is the opposite.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Völkisch and some strands did so, but Italian and French cores did not centrally.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Hierarchy and exclusion of Jews, Protestants and foreigners as Anti-France deny equal worth.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not relevant to a movement rejecting socialism; neutral.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Imperial expansion and settlement sought; Corradini wanted outlets for emigration.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: No source documents a position on religious personal law for these movements.

restrict-conversion.rationale: No source documents a position on conversion; Maurras valued Catholicism socially but was agnostic.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not an issue in these contexts; inferred no.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Maurras saw the Church as an ideological agent of the central state, so religious instruction fits.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authoritarian leader and rejection of parliamentary democracy deny that legitimacy rests on consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Industrial state building for imperial competition fits mercantilist outlook.

population-transfer.rationale: Exclusion of Anti-France groups and xenophobia lead to support for removal of hostile minorities, though not explicit.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Glorifying violence and imperial war directly contradict it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Corradini cast international struggle between nations as the driver, with iron discipline and ruthlessness.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: These movements opposed the liberal order and themselves would be banned; neutral.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is liberal; inferred rejection.

separated-powers.rationale: Anti-parliamentarism and a leader with absolute power go against checks and balances.

vanguard-party.rationale: Corradini borrowed socialist tactics, but vanguard of the working class is an anti-nationalist doctrine.

priority-to-poor.rationale: National producers' unity, not poor priority, was the aim.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Corporatism aimed to end class conflict and so would curtail strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Corradini argued Italian poverty came from exploitation by plutocratic nations, not numbers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Integral nationalism holds that unassimilable groups are Anti-France.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contrary to the leader principle and hierarchy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authoritarian anti-leftist movements justified exceptional measures against internal enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price fixing is not documented; corporatist bodies later set prices, but the early programme is silent.

party-controls-media.rationale: Proto-fascists generally lacked totalitarian ambitions, so media control by a ruling party is less central.

party-commands-army.rationale: The ANI supported the monarchy as head of the armed forces, not party control.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Xenophobic exclusion implies a long wait or no citizenship.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; elitist outlook suggests no.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Corradini demanded iron discipline and cohesion.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Nationalists opposed supranational limits on national sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: ANI monarchism and authoritarianism favour the executive head commanding forces and choosing ministers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Maurras favoured the Catholic Church as an institution, but not a stated stance on its governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Maurras and others used the church for order, but did not seek clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Corradini attacked socialist anti-patriotism and anti-militarism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Maurrasian moralism would say yes but Futurists opposed moralism; split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Leader with absolute power implies no term limits.

recall-officials.rationale: Parliamentary mechanisms of the democratic sort were rejected.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Imperial expansion and military power favour alliances such as Italian wartime moves, not withdrawal.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; no support for such a socialist-style measure.

people-in-arms.rationale: Paramilitary leagues and Arditi valued armed volunteers, but the ANI wanted a strong regular army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Blood and Soil romanticism and Maurras agrarianism said yes, while Futurists and industrial nationalists exalted cities.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Italian irredentism sought to bring Italian-populated lands into the kingdom.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectual cult of action; not documented specifically.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Exclusive nationalism and imperialism regard their own nation as superior.

death-penalty.rationale: Movements honouring violence and order favoured harsh punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Opposition to feminism and gender equality is stated by Futurist Marinetti.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; nationalists were split between Catholic and secular.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Maurrasian moralism says yes, Futurists no; split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnic and exclusivist nationalism favours descent-based citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Nationalists favoured national cultural uniformity, though Maurras defended regional privileges.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Protestants and Jews were treated as Anti-France; exemptions unlikely.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Order, hierarchy and subordination of the individual deny it, though the Futurists were avant-garde.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Corradini attacked plutocracies exploiting proletarian nations, so cancelling debts fits; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Corradini linked national power and economic exploitation, but not property transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Parliamentary democracy was rejected, so a constituent assembly is unattractive.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The ANI authoritarian corporate state subordinated freedoms to national industrial power.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: National competition with no humanitarian duty beyond borders.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic, but military superiority and independence would favour it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Leader worship may favour acclamation, but not documented.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The state controlling economy implies no independent banks.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Irredentism and expansion oppose giving up claimed lands.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Corporatism subordinates property to national interest.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliances yes for power but binding automatic commitment unaddressed.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Maurras used the Church for the state's purposes while Catholic nationalists resisted; split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Absolute value of national unity justifies force.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: ANI monarchism and Maurras monarchy embody national unity above parties.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Centralized nation-state unity; Maurras alone favoured regional liberties.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The ANI supported a constitutional monarchy, not a sacred ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax-rate structure is not addressed in any consulted source on these movements.

character-from-environment.rationale: Eugenic and Blood and Soil ideas stress innate national and racial nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A single leader with absolute power is a shared trait.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; Futurist taste for expansion but unaddressed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Monarchy plus corporate assembly has a mixed shape, but not documented as doctrine.

leader-cult.rationale: Favouring a single leader with absolute power is a listed trait, and the leader cult follows.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not addressed in the sources; traditional-family views point in no clear direction.

land-redistribution.rationale: Maurras defended traditional property and the ANI membership was wealthy.

refugee-return.rationale: Exclusionary nationalism opposes returns of minorities or descendants.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Italian irredentism claimed lands because Italians lived there.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not documented; Maurras was agnostic himself.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not documented; Western nationalists did not require veils.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-movements existed among some but integral nationalists prioritised the single nation.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minorities are Anti-France or must be absorbed, so separate institutions are rejected.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not documented; would not endorse minority emancipation.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Willpower and myth, not economic determinism, drive history for these thinkers.

ban-cartels.rationale: Corporatism organises producers into state-recognised bodies, rather than breaking them up.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not addressed; state-guided industry suggests support, anti-plutocrat rhetoric the opposite.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Hostile to liberal constraints; leader and nation above them.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Futurist manifesto opposes feminism, so parity is rejected.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Imperial industrial state leaning on its own bloc fits autarkic imperial outlook.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Supranational standards run against national sovereignty.

moral-incentives.rationale: Duty and sacrifice to the nation featured, though capitalist incentives persisted.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Arditi, Freikorps and Sorel stressed small violent elites; D'Annunzio's raid is typical.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Maurras and the monarchist ANI defended hierarchy and monarchy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Integral nationalism puts the nation first.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Imperial nationalists justified colonial rule, as Crispi did.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; opponents of racial remedies but no documented position.

patriotic-education.rationale: The nation as absolute value requires patriotic instruction.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary institutions are not addressed in the consulted sources on these movements.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Corradini accepted capitalism with national direction, so crisis not inevitable.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperialists such as the ANI sought influence abroad, with Italian irredentism.

delink-world-market.rationale: Corradini wanted proletarian nations to challenge the plutocracies by conquest, not withdrawal.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Rejects Marxist exploitation analysis, though does cast rich nations as exploiters.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Exclusionary but state-directed; not private-property libertarian.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Anti-liberal, leader-centred movements rejected constitutional limits.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Treaty validity is not addressed; irredentists did reject borders they saw as unjust, but the sources are silent.

elective-rulers.rationale: ANI supported monarchy and rejected parliamentary politics.

minority-veto.rationale: Leadership principle and authority contradict it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Absolute leader and monarchy, not resisting rulers; though Maurras prized law.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: No source documents an animal-welfare position for these movements; left neutral.

animal-use-humane.rationale: No source documents an animal-use position for these movements; left neutral.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Hierarchical Maurrasian order stressed duties of elites; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Maurras slogan Politics first, and cult of action reject withdrawal.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist state is not their model; inferred only that they reject the socialist premise of the claim.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Corradini's central doctrine that nationalism is the socialism of exploited nations, redirecting class struggle into imperialist war.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: the Futurists and nationalists wanted culture to mobilise the nation for struggle and attacked passivity, and the pacification thesis is a left-critical frame they would not adopt.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: these movements held that order rests on authority, hierarchy and discipline, and scorned the liberal bourgeois elite as weak rather than as hegemonic through culture.

native-born-offices.rationale: Maurras's integral nationalism excluded foreigners, Jews and other 'Anti-France' groups from the nation's institutions, which implies reserving office to natives.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from nationalism: they opposed foreign direction of national movements, though they were anti-socialist and did not address communist parties as such.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: Corradini's proletarian nation sought strength through national struggle and expansion, not dependence on richer powers' aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The Italian Nationalist Association's programme was irredentist, demanding the 'unredeemed' lands such as Trentino, Trieste and Dalmatia.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the ANI backed colonial empire and hierarchy, so ranking colonised peoples' descendants over settlers cuts against their imperialism.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: as precursors whose heirs built fascism, they rejected liberal-democratic constitutionalism and would oppose enshrining anti-fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: they were fiercely anti-socialist but glorified their own strong authority, so they would reject being condemned alongside communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: These movements never addressed the American Civil War and no source places them on it; adherents have no principled stance.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from their reverence for national tradition and heroes; Maurrassian nationalism treats the national past as a heritage to defend.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred: Futurism despised feminism and exalted masculine strength, so they would not see men as a disadvantaged group needing programmes.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from Marinetti's contempt for women and feminism and a hierarchical view of the sexes; equal-services claims would not be adopted.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Maurras and the ANI rejected imported liberal parliamentarism as foreign to the national tradition and favoured institutions rooted in each nation's history.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the ANI's militarism and monarchism and Futurism's glorification of war; a political role for the army as order's guardian fits.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: corporatist class collaboration and Futurist contempt for feminism leave no room for wages-for-housework demands.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the family strand's emphasis on hierarchy, duty and the nation as an extended family.

office-by-exam.rationale: Split: the movements favoured elite rule against parliament and patronage but did not make examinations the route.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from economic nationalism: Corradini's proletarian nation put the national interest above open markets.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, Catholic-leaning family stance of Maurras and the Italian Nationalists.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Italian Nationalist Association and Action Francaise rejected parliamentary democracy and favoured strong, unaccountable authority.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from corporatism and state-organised class collaboration, which sits against purely individual private accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: land is subordinated to national interest, but private ownership was not attacked.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from anti-parliamentarism: budget control by an elected parliament was part of what they rejected.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the integral nationalist demand for national homogeneity and exclusion of minorities.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from nativism and the demand that the nation's soil stay in national hands.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from hierarchical, anti-egalitarian nationalism that judged groups by national or racial standing, not equal outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the anti-bourgeois, anti-materialist rhetoric of Corradini and Marinetti.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the glorification of war and imperialism and irredentist agitation against rival states.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the imperialism and national-power doctrine of the Italian Nationalists, which subordinated other states' choices.

corporate-influence.rationale: Corporatist class collaboration meant state-coordinated business, but no source addresses lobbying; inferred as split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Nation-above-all nationalists distrusted foreign influence; inferred from their anti-internationalism.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Corradini's imperialist proletarian nation wanted population strength for national struggle; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Integral nationalists favoured protecting the national community and its land from outsiders; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Proto-fascists wanted class peace under the state but no source documents a job guarantee.

democratic-peace.rationale: They rejected liberal democracy and glorified war, so spreading democracy for peace is the opposite of their view.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: They demanded iron discipline and authority, and nation above the individual leaves no right to disobey.

non-intervention.rationale: Imperialist nationalists such as Corradini sought expansion and war, which rejects a bar on intervention; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: The ANI backed unions and economic bodies organised by trade within a corporatist state; the industry-versus-craft question is inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Maurras cast Jews, Protestants, Masons and foreigners as an Anti-France; scapegoating minorities is a documented trait.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: They defended traditional family and hierarchy, so no abolition of legal marriage; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Authoritarian, hierarchical nationalists favoured state secrecy over a legal access right; inferred.

local-production.rationale: National economic strength mattered but no source addresses local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: They favoured disciplined hierarchy, a single leader and permanent organisation, not informal trust groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Nation above all and rejection of liberal internationalism imply national law over international courts; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Maurrassians were Catholic-friendly while Futurists were anti-clerical, so the strands are split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Nationalists wanted their nation to rise and lead, not to defer to another power; inferred from ANI imperialism.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Integral nationalism put a unified nation and centralised authority above regions; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The corporatist model kept private property and sought class collaboration rather than common ownership of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Proto-fascist movements were anti-socialist and treated Marxist class struggle as a threat to the nation.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery is not documented in these movements; inferred as indifferent.

religion-illusion.rationale: Maurras valued Catholicism as social order and Futurists scorned the church, so none treated religion as a mere illusion; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Corradini accepted capitalist production as a necessary engine of national power; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Futurist manifesto expressed contempt for women and feminism, and nationalists defended hierarchy.

socialized-care.rationale: Nationalist doctrine kept the family as the national cell, not a public service; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Futurists and nationalists campaigned against foreign influence on Italian culture; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Proto-fascists subordinated legal restraints to national interest; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The movements were nation-state centred and corporatist, opposed to commune-based society.

majority-settlement.rationale: Irredentism and imperialism implied settling and binding conquered territories to the nation; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Corradini and the ANI offered corporatism and national solidarity as an alternative to liberal capitalism and socialism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Integral nationalists grounded the nation in tradition and history, inferring a mild yes; no source addresses competing land claims directly.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic: the Holocaust postdates the movements; their antisemitism is documented but denial is not.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Maurras-style traditionalism disapproved of homosexuality, but no source documents a call for criminalization; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Proto-fascists rejected parliamentary democracy and favoured strong authority, and Freikorps and nationalist groups attacked socialist opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Maurras supported the Church as social order while personally agnostic; adherents split, inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Italian Nationalist Association was openly imperialist and sought colonies, as Libya, for national benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as a mild no from the movements' European nationalist focus.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; proto-fascists put the nation above religion, inferred against religious-law legitimacy tests.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Proto-fascists rejected parliamentary democracy and direct popular rule in favour of strong authority.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Corradini replaced class struggle with national struggle, so analyses of overlapping oppression are inferred as strongly rejected.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; the movements' traditionalism and hostility to liberalism infer a firm no.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred against from their traditional-nation outlook.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: They claimed to transcend liberalism and socialism by joining nationalism with elements of both, though not in the Third Way sense; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Proto-fascists rejected class conflict and favoured class collaboration; the Marxist concept is inferred as rejected.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Integral nationalists regarded outsiders as Anti-France; the claim about Islam is inferred from that exclusion.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Maurras grounded authority in tradition and nation rather than popular will, but not always in God; adherents split.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; Maurras valued Catholic tradition as social order, so no clear direction is inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: The ANI endorsed Rocco's corporatism to end class conflict, a state-managed third path between laissez-faire and socialism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Marinetti's Manifesto glorifies war and the military spirit; the movement is strongly opposed to disarmament.

rich-first.rationale: Corradini's proletarian nation argued that Italy should win a place among richer powers by national struggle, a variant of the rise-first idea; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The ANI pushed Italy toward imperial expansion and alliance with great powers over neutrality; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Not addressed; monarchists such as the Italian Nationalists accepted dynastic rule, while later fascism relied on a single leader chosen by struggle.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred; corporatist class collaboration favored state-guided or producer-bloc credit, not user-owned mutual banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from Corradini's proletarian nation, which cast poorer nations as exploited by richer powers and urged them to resist.

property-franchise.rationale: Not addressed directly; the movements rejected parliamentary democracy, but their views on a restricted franchise varied.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred; Futurism glorified mastery and violence and scorned women and feminism, which runs against ending both dominations.

reification.rationale: Inferred; these movements rejected Marxism and its class analysis, preferring national unity and myth to a critique of market fetishism.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred; they sought class collaboration and a strong state, and showed little interest in the claim that wealth hollows out press freedom.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: They rejected liberal constitutionalism for strong authority and a single leader, and glorified action over legal restraint.

racial-franchise.rationale: Integral nationalism and the Italian Nationalists excluded Jews, foreigners and others from the national tradition, which implies a restricted political community.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the internet postdates these movements and no position can be inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from their authoritarian preference for strong leadership and contempt for parliamentary scrutiny.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred; Maurras's exclusion of Jews and Protestants as Anti-France suggests support for limits on marriage across religions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred; Action Francaise's hostility to Jews as outsiders fits an economic shunning of their businesses, though the sources do not describe boycotts.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Proto-fascists rejected parliament and popular deliberation in favor of authority, elites and corporate bodies, so rule by citizens chosen by lot is inferred as strongly opposed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Integral nationalists like Maurras defended inherited Catholic tradition as national order, so reinterpreting doctrine for modernity is inferred as disfavored, though Futurists scorned religion.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Proto-fascists attacked class conflict rather than wealth as such, and favoured corporatist collaboration with owners; adherents split, so neutral.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, militarist, authoritarian values these movements celebrated; the sources do not discuss sexual orientation.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Integral nationalists like Maurras defended the Catholic Church as a national institution, so state atheism would be rejected; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: These movements glorified violence and war and favoured strong authority, so abolishing police and prisons runs against their core.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Integral nationalism demanded one unified nation under strong authority, which is hostile to power-sharing among communities; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from corporatist preference for state-organised class collaboration over voluntary private relief.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from the preference for strong, lasting authority over parliamentary rotation.

vote-delegation.rationale: They rejected parliamentary democracy and favoured strong authority, so a citizen-delegation system conflicts with their principles.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The issue is anachronistic and outside the movements' concerns.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, Catholic-aligned and hierarchical views of integral nationalists.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the patriarchal, hierarchical social order these movements favoured.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Proto-fascist nationalists put the nation and its citizens first and distrusted foreigners, so extending local votes to foreign residents is inferred as a no.

rent-control.rationale: Corporatist class collaboration allowed state intervention, but no source documents a rent position; inferred as indifferent.

abolish-ip.rationale: Corporatist nationalists such as Rocco defended property and national production as national assets; abolition is inferred as unlikely, though it was not discussed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Proto-fascists glorified martial virtue and youth (Marinetti's Futurism, nationalist youth cults), and fascism later institutionalised uniformed youth organisations, so a yes is inferred from the family's outlook.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic for pre-1914 movements; no position exists and the issue cannot be inferred either way.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Proto-fascists prized national sovereignty and strength, so foreign bases would be seen as an affront; inferred, though some favoured alliances.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The recognition debate is anachronistic for these movements, and their scapegoating of minorities makes it unlikely they would favour it, but it was not addressed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Corradini's proletarian nation and corporatism rewarded national productive work yet defended private property, so adherents sit between the two.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Proto-fascists glorified violence and war and held force justified in defence of the nation, so condemning killing even in self-defence is firmly rejected (Manifesto of Futurism praises war).

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Integral nationalism and Corradini's nationalism stressed the nation as an organic, enduring entity with a continuous tradition, so continuity is central.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not discussed; the movements' traditional gender order and biological nationalism imply rejection, inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not discussed; the movements' traditional gender order implies rejection, inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Proto-fascist thought cultivated the cult of the nation's fallen and of heroic sacrifice, as in Futurism's glorification of war and the later fascist cult of the fallen.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Integral nationalism and Maurras's Action Francaise tied the nation to religious tradition and a struggle against decadence, so a mild yes is inferred, though many were secular.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The statement concerns diaspora, which was not a theme; Italian nationalists did however seek expansion, so it does not fit.

culture-before-state.rationale: Proto-fascists wanted a strong state and national power as the vehicle for national renewal, so putting culture first is inferred as rejected, though Futurists emphasised cultural revolution.

god-not-male.rationale: Not discussed; traditionalist religion within integral nationalism implies a rejection, inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not discussed; its traditionalist outlook implies a rejection, inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Nationalists of this family put the national majority first and scapegoated minorities, so a lean to yes is inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Irredentism existed in Italian nationalism but the statement is about merging regions for one people; no stated view, so inferred as split.

missingStatements.text: A state should replace parliament with a legislature of unions and economic bodies organised by trade.
missingStatements.rationale: The ANI endorsed Rocco's corporate state with an assembly of unions and economic bodies in place of parliament, to end class conflict.

missingStatements.text: Italy and similar nations are proletarian nations exploited by richer powers, and should win a place through national struggle.
missingStatements.rationale: Corradini's central doctrine that nationalism is the socialism of exploited nations, redirecting class struggle into imperialist war.

missingStatements.text: Jews, foreigners and other groups that cannot belong to the national tradition should be excluded from the nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Maurras treated Protestants, Jews, Freemasons and foreigners as Anti-France who could never be integrated.

notes: Family label with divergent strands: Futurists were modernist and anti-clerical while Maurrassians were traditionalist and Catholic-friendly, so answers on religion, heritage and ruralism are split. Several answers are inferred.
